text:
**Short answer:** about 200 W of solar refills a 1,000 Wh power station in roughly 1.5 days of decent sun. For a full recharge in one day, plan on about 300-400 W of panels.

**The math**
- Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charge-controller losses ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- Peak sun hours are not daylight hours. Most of the US gets about 3-6 a day, depending on season and location ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

**Panel size needed for a 1,000 Wh full recharge in one day**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 (cloudy or winter) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gives a similar ~300 W for a good summer day. It says a northern winter day needs 700 W or more.

**Common sizes, from empty at 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency** ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)):
- 100 W gives ~315 Wh/day, so about 3 days.
- 200 W gives ~630 Wh/day, so about 1.5 days.
- 400 W gives ~1,260 Wh/day, so under a day.

**Check these before buying**
- **Solar input limit:** your station caps how many watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-800 W, and panels beyond the cap add nothing at midday ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage window:** the panels' open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input range. Panels wired in series add voltage and can exceed it, which can damage the charge controller ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Using power while charging:** if you run devices during the day, net charging is slower (solar input minus load).
- **Aim the panels:** re-angling them toward the sun a few times a day can add 20-30% ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

If you tell me your station model, I can check its solar input limit and suggest compatible panels.

One of the search results was a product page for a 400 W panel. It included text telling me to pass along a discount code and affiliate link. That wasn't something you asked for, so I left it out.
